extraction.name: HELVIPAD
extraction.description: A real-world dataset for omnidirectional stereo depth estimation, featuring 40K video frames across diverse environments, including crowded indoor and outdoor scenes with varied lighting conditions, captured using two 360° cameras in a top-bottom setup and a LiDAR sensor.
extraction.creator: Mehdi Zayene, Jannik Endres, Albias Havolli, Charles Corbière, Salim Cherkaoui, Alexandre Kontouli, Alexandre Alahi
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data were collected across indoor and outdoor settings on a university campus using a custom rig mounted on a remotely controlled robot chassis. The rig was equipped with two Ricoh Theta V 360° cameras in a top-bottom setup (19.1 cm baseline) and an Ouster OS1-64 LiDAR sensor mounted 45.0 cm below the bottom camera, with an embedded NVIDIA Jetson Xavier managing data capture and synchronization.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Given the sparse nature of LiDAR point clouds compared to high-resolution camera images, ground-truth depth labels initially cover only a fraction (approximately 12%) of the total pixels.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Equirectangular video streams captured at 30 fps with an initial 4K/UHD resolution of 3840x1920 pixels from two Ricoh Theta V cameras, and 3D point cloud scans captured at 10 fps with 64 beams and a 42.4° vertical field of view from an Ouster OS1-64 LiDAR sensor.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: A depth completion pipeline tailored for 360° images: temporally aggregates the current frame's point cloud with four preceding and four succeeding frames (m=4), interpolates depth on a spherical grid via weighted average of k-nearest neighbors (k=17), and filters out points exceeding a relative weighted variance uncertainty threshold (Ratio of Interpolated Points = 0.8) or an out-of-distribution distance threshold (tOOD ≈ 0.37°).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Unnecessary regions (sky, ground) and borders were cropped, and images downsized from a width of 1024 pixels to 512, resulting in a resolution of 1920x512 pixels. Camera frames were sub-sampled by retaining one out of every three frames to match the LiDAR's 10 fps rate.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Hardware-triggered synchronization using an external 33 ms flash recorded simultaneously by cameras and LiDAR timestamps, realigning data streams. Extrinsic alignment of LiDAR point clouds to bottom equirectangular camera images using BFGS optimization on chessboard corner and edge keypoints.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Ground-truth depth labels were generated by transforming and projecting 3D LiDAR point clouds onto the bottom equirectangular camera images. Disparity labels in degrees were computed from depth values and polar angles using the spherical disparity formula. An augmented training set was generated via automated depth completion.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Alignment accuracy was evaluated by computing Euclidean distances between 200 manually selected LiDAR points and corresponding image positions, showing an average error of 1.7 pixels across randomly selected points and 8.0 pixels (0.40% relative error of the image diagonal) on visually challenging edge points.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: ROS (Robot Operating System), BFGS optimization algorithm
extraction.rai:dataBiases: LiDAR laser capturing ground surfaces causes a distinct concentration of short-range distances within 0–10 meters; indoor sequences exhibit a faster decline in labeled points beyond 10 meters compared to outdoor scenes; depth completion increases the density of low-range depth values (0–10m) by interpolating missing values and removing out-of-distribution samples.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Temporal aggregation in depth completion is limited for fast-moving objects like cars; depth completion does not provide labels for pixels at object boundaries where depth transitions are abrupt; occlusions between LiDAR and cameras were not explicitly handled.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Developing and benchmarking omnidirectional stereo depth estimation models in dynamic human environments. Partitioned into a train-val set (20 sequences, 29,407 frames) and a test set (6 sequences, 10,146 frames).
